tasks.title: Fireball
tasks.statement: A fireball was observed from three different observing sites I, II, III. The position of the observing sites, the altitude and azimuth of start and end points of the fireball’s trajectory are given in Table 1. Azimuth is measured eastward from the North direction, and altitude measured above the horizon, and both the angular measurements are in degrees. Following the steps below, find true trajectory and location on the surface of Earth of fallen debris of the fireball (meteorite). Table 1. Observational Data for a Fireball: I (127.3°E, +35.7°, start: azimuth 17°, altitude 35°, end: azimuth 77°, altitude 10°); II (128.5°E, +37.0°, start: azimuth 235°, altitude -, end: azimuth 139°, altitude -); III (128.5°E, +35.4°, start: azimuth 325°, altitude -, end: azimuth 48°, altitude -).

parts.question: You are provided by a scaled marked graph paper. Mark the 3 observing positions (I, II, III) and draw a projected trajectory of the fireball as seen on the surface of Earth.
parts.reference: Marking points I, II, III correctly. Marking and drawing the fireball trajectory correctly – 3 pts.

parts.question: Calculate the longitude and latitude of start (A, A) and end (B, B) points of the fireball and total length L of the trajectory projected on the earth surface.
parts.reference: Getting longitude and latitude of Points A, B correctly. Getting distance with correct scaling over longitude and latitude – 2 pts.

parts.question: Find the heights of starting point hA and end point hB. of the fireball’s trajectory above the surface of Earth.
parts.reference: Getting the right geometry. Final values of heights within 10 percent of error – 3 pts.

parts.question: Where can you find a meteorite, if it survives passage through the atmosphere and hits the ground? Calculate the longitude and latitude (C, C) of the location of the meteorite on the surface of Earth’s. Finally, redraw the table to your answer-book and fill the empty cells with your results.
parts.reference: Getting the right geometry. Final values of the correct position within 10 percent of error – 2 pts.

tasks.title: Moon
tasks.statement: The Korean Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI) publishes the Korean Astronomical Almanac every year. You have been provided with an astronomical table extracted from the Korean Astronomical Almanac of 2012 showing the Korean local time of Moon culmination.

parts.question: Find the date in April 2012 when the Moon is closest to the Earth.
Find the date in March 2012 when the Moon is remotest from the Earth.

The scaled marked graph paper (a) shows the eccentric orbit of the Moon, the Earth being located at the center. Mark the positions of the Moon by the symbol XX on April 19 and April 23 (with labels A19 and A23).
parts.reference: Similar to the Figure in the answer sheet – 2 pts, ± 10 degrees – 1 pt.

parts.question: Calculate the ratio of the apparent angular sizes of the Moon (Moon) and the Sun (Sun) on July 1.
Draw on the scaled marked graph paper the geostationary orbit around the Earth in the given scale.
parts.reference: Similar to the figure in the solutions – 2 pts, radius less than 1 cm – 1 pts.
